Answer: C
Reason: The arrow points to a widened left superior mediastinum, which, in the context of mild hypoxaemia and dyspnoea without pulmonary congestion, is characteristic of a Persistent Left Superior Vena Cava (PLSVC) draining into the left atrium. This anomaly creates a right-to-left shunt, explaining the hypoxaemia, while the "slight enlargement of the left ventricle" may actually represent the dilated coronary sinus or be a misinterpretation of the vascular shadow associated with this congenital defect.
